calls.head: Washington lets teams in close, and Tampa Bay goes there
calls.body: Washington has struggled to keep shots to the perimeter (24th of 32), and Tampa Bay makes its shots count: one expected goal for every 15.3 unblocked shots, 7th in the league.
calls.call: Tampa Bay needs no more than its usual 15.3 unblocked shots per expected goal.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: Tampa Bay needed 15.0 unblocked shots per expected goal, against its usual 15.3.

calls.head: Tampa Bay hounds the puck; Washington sits back
calls.body: On forecheck pressure, Tampa Bay sits 9th of 32, at the hounding end of the scale. Washington is 30th, at the passive end.
calls.call: Tampa Bay puts more forecheck pressure on than Washington.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On forecheck score (arena-adjusted, 100 is league average), Tampa Bay had 139 and Washington 92. Coming in, Tampa Bay was at 103 and Washington at 85.

TBL.head: We gave Tampa Bay a 67% chance, and Tampa Bay delivered.

WSH.head: We gave Washington only a 33% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Washington was kept to the outside
surprises.body: Washington needed 22.5 unblocked shots per expected goal at 5-on-5, against its usual 14.9 and a league average of 15.8. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 40 games.

surprises.head: Tampa Bay tried a different line
surprises.body: B. Point, G. Goncalves, N. Kucherov played 9:58 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Tampa Bay’s usual lines.
